changes.comment: createHttpTransport takes an optional authProvider (McpOAuthClientProvider, the SDK's OAuthClientProvider under this package's name) for MCP servers that require OAuth 2.1. The interactive steps (state, saveCodeVerifier, redirectToAuthorization) run only inside connectMcpSession; on a later call, the SDK's background reconnect of the event stream, or close they are refused and the operation fails 'unauthorized'. redirectToAuthorization is also refused for a URL that is neither https: nor http: on a loopback host. The 'unauthorized' reason gains resourceMetadataUrl, the validated resource_metadata URL from the endpoint's WWW-Authenticate challenge. An OAuth error from the authorization server now classifies as 'unauthorized'. Failure messages no longer carry server-authored text: an 'unauthorized' failure, or one from an HTTP or OAuth error, reads as its kind and status (e.g. "unauthorized (HTTP 401)", "transport (HTTP 500)"), because a server may repeat a credential. Static headers are now applied by the package's egress wrapper, only to requests for the MCP endpoint's origin (overriding a same-named header there, as before), and never to the authorization server or any other origin; the SDK is no longer given them. createHttpTransport refuses a static header named twice in different letter cases, and fails with fixed text when building the transport throws (an invalid header, or an authProvider member that throws). Static headers are copied when createHttpTransport is called; later changes to the caller's record have no effect. A fetch getter that throws fails createHttpTransport with fixed text.
